svg.title: How a plug-in obtains and uses the Organization service
svg.desc: The plug-in asks the service provider for IOrganizationServiceFactory. CreateOrganizationService with context.UserId returns a service that acts as the step's user and is limited by that user's security roles. CreateOrganizationService with null returns a service that acts as the SYSTEM user and is not limited by the caller's roles. Each call on a service, such as Retrieve, RetrieveMultiple, Create, Update, Delete or Execute, is a new message that runs through its own event pipeline with depth increased by one. When the calling step is synchronous in stage 20 or 40, the nested operation is part of the same database transaction, so an error in it rolls back everything.
svg.text: From the service provider to a data operation: Omar resolves a case
1. Plug-in step (Depth 1)
Close / incident / PreOperation
synchronous, inside the transaction
Execute(serviceProvider)
2. IOrganizationServiceFactory
Requested by type from the provider.
Creates a service for one identity.
CreateOrganizationService(id)
3a. Service as the user: context.UserId
Acts as Omar (or the step's "Run in User's Context" user).
Security roles, sharing and column security apply.
Use for: anything done on the user's behalf.
Cedar: read the case being resolved, default the service line.
3b. Service as SYSTEM: null
Acts as the built-in SYSTEM user: sees and changes every row.
The caller's roles do not limit it. Created by = SYSTEM.
Use for: a rule that must hold whatever the caller may read.
Cedar: count open work orders. Disclose only the count.
4. Every call is a new message with its own pipeline (Depth 2)
Retrieve RetrieveMultiple Create Update Delete Associate Execute
Other plug-ins registered on that message and table run too. No Web API, no sign-in:
the user is already authenticated.
5. One transaction
Called from a synchronous step in stage 20 or 40, the nested operation joins the caller's transaction and sees its uncommitted changes.
If a nested operation fails, the whole transaction ends. Catching the error and continuing is not possible: report it or let it fail.
